subject: gk
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution pertains to the Fundamental Duties?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51-A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51-A** pertains to the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens.
 
• It was added to the Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have certain duties to perform towards their country and society.
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under Article 51-A.
 
• These duties include respecting the Constitution, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India, and promoting harmony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **42nd Amendment Act**, also known as the "Mini-Constitution," made significant changes to the Indian Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
 
• Although the Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law, they serve as moral obligations for every citizen.
 
• The idea behind these duties is to encourage responsible behavior and promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was appointed to make recommendations about Fundamental Duties, and many of its suggestions were incorporated into Article 51-A.
